about: Every slot of the film, in order. A slot with no clip renders a labelled slate, so the film always plays. Times are seconds from the start of the film. The story is demo-video/docs/STORY.md; the nine AI shots and their hand-over are demo-video/docs/SHOTS.md.

slots.shows: Daytime, a bright office. A colleague looks up from her phone, pleasantly surprised: her answer came, and it is 2 AM where he lives.
Late afternoon, another city, a small meeting room. A colleague glances at the wall screen: his update is already there.
Evening, a third place, a home desk under a lamp. A colleague leans back, half laughing, and asks if he ever sleeps.
Cut to night. He is fast asleep.
The night room. His phone lights up for a meeting. A double of him, made of mint light, rises out of him, stands, and pulls the blanket over his shoulder.
The double walks to the desk, sits and opens the laptop. The screen lights its face. A small AI Peer tag glows on its chest.
The camera pushes into the laptop screen, into the real product. Made by code from the last frame of reveal-desk.
The real meeting. It joins as a labelled AI, says it is an AI, gives his update, answers a question, and brings back what needs his judgment.
Real Slack at night. A colleague's question, answered with its sources, and no promise made for him.
The other direction. One change elsewhere in the company that touches his project, caught and brought to him.
The same room at sunrise, warm light through the window. He wakes rested, sits up and picks up his phone.
The morning brief from the real product: what the Peer did, what it learned, and the one thing that needs him.
He reads the brief on his phone and decides with one tap.
By the desk in daylight, the double, now faint, nods to him and fades away.
The camera pulls out of one lit window, over the city, up to the Earth from space. On the night side, mint lights come on across the dark cities.
The AI Peer mark, the line "More room for your best work.", and "Built for real this week".

narration.about: Where each spoken line starts, in film seconds. A hook line whose shot arrives lip-synced takes its time from the clip instead (SHOTS.md, line_at_s).
